title: nebula-telemetry-mixed-profile-sla-run-synthesis-2029-11
content:
Executive summary:

This note synthesizes the week-long benchmarking runs we executed for Nebula Telemetry (edge-heavy telemetry ingestion + conversational alert triage). Goal was to validate that a Redwood Dedicated configuration (r5-dedicated pool with mixed A100 and H100 nodes, instance-level autoscale) can meet Nebula’s latency SLOs while staying within their committed cost envelope. Runs were executed 2029-11-18 -> 2029-11-23 across three mixed-profile workloads.

High-level outcomes (short):
- Primary SLOs: conversational p95 <= 220ms, ingestion inference p95 <= 85ms. We met ingestion SLO on warm caches; conversational p95 hit 240–260ms on baseline config (slightly above SLO).
- Tail sensitivity: cold-start microbursts and KV-cache-miss paths dominated p99 and produced intermittent SLA violations.
- Cost: projected monthly bill (steady 12k qps ingestion + 600 conv qps business tier) is ~$38k/mo on the current profile; with recommended batching + cache tuning ~20–28% savings estimated.
- Recommendation: enable aggressive prefix caching for ingestion, instrument route-based batching for conv path, and roll out model-quantization candidate (4-bit) to a canary 10% pool.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Nebula acceptance criteria defined in kickoff:
  - Ingestion model (short classification) p95 <= 85ms across 95% of 12-hour windows
  - Conversational model p95 <= 220ms with 99.9% availability
  - Cost per 1M tokens (inference + infra) <= $120
  - No single microburst should cause >5 minutes of degraded route availability

Testbed and configs used (summary):
- Redwood Dedicated pool: 6 x H100-80GB + 10 x A100-40GB, node weight routing (H100 favored for conv hotshard), 2 dedicated subnet zones.
- Model variants: telemetry-classify-v2 (2.7B fp16), conv-llm-v1 (13B fp16), conv-llm-q4a (13B quant candidate).
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime 1.9.4 with continuous batching enabled, KV prefix cache warmup scripts used.
- Traffic generator: custom harness (github repo referenced above) that replays production traces with synthetic bursts (burst-factor=5, burst-duration=90s), background steady QPS, and cold-start scenarios (cache TTL flush every 30m).
- Metrics captured: token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency per route, queue depth, batch sizes, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, model load times, and tail GC events.

Workload profiles tested:
1) Ingestion-heavy steady: 12,000 qps classification requests, median request size 48 tokens, expected to be extremely latency sensitive.
2) Conversational mixed: 600 qps new-turns, 1.8k qps context-append requests; average conv length 120 tokens (input+output), KV cache expected to reduce work for context-append.
3) Mixed microburst day: baseline steady traffic (ingestion 6k qps, conv 300 qps) with scheduled microbursts (x5) to simulate flash events from telemetry spikes.

Key observational findings:
- Ingestion path (telemetry-classify-v2): warm-cache p95 = 62ms, p99 = 98ms. Cold-cache p95 spikes to 220–300ms for first 30s after TTL flush. Observed that continuous-batching lowered per-request overhead; however tiny-batch fallback triggered often under burst shedding reducing batch efficiency.
- Conversational path (conv-llm-v1 fp16): with H100 routing, baseline p95 = 240ms, p99 = 420ms. Major contributor: KV cache misses for long contexts and backend model attention recompute. When routing to H100 and boosting batch-window to 40ms, p95 dropped to ~210ms but queue depth and tail p99 moved higher during bursts.
- Quantized variant (conv-llm-q4a): average inference latency decreased ~18% on H100 but exhibited occasional 1.5x latency jitter on A100 nodes due to kernel fallback paths. Accuracy regression measured on Nebula prompt set: ~0.9 BLEU-equivalent relative drop (within Nebula tolerance threshold).
- Cost breakdown: token compute dominates (72%), idle GPU amortization 18%, networking and IO 10%. Enabling 4-bit quantization and route steering yields estimated compute savings of 22% for conv workload.

Failure modes and root causes observed:
- Cold-start cascade: when multiple shards load the conv model simultaneously during a sustained burst, SLO violations cascade due to synchronous TorchLoader delays. Mitigation: staggered model loading and pre-warm orchestration across pool.
- Microburst batch collapse: very short, high magnitude bursts led to small batches and poor throughput; batching window tuning helped but increased p50 under steady-state. Tradeoff documented below.
- Hybrid-hardware variability: A100 nodes with older CUDA stacks surfaced kernel fallbacks for quantized ops; hardware-aware routing is needed.

Performance tables (representative numbers extracted from runs):
- Ingestion steady (12k qps) warm-cache: p50=28ms, p95=62ms, p99=98ms, avg batch size=6, GPU util=43%
- Ingestion cold-window (first 30s post-TTL): p95=240ms, p99=410ms, model load spikes observed
- Conversational baseline (H100 preferred): p50=120ms, p95=240ms, p99=420ms, avg batch size=4
- Conversational with 40ms batching window: p50=150ms, p95=210ms, p99=560ms (during bursts), avg batch size=6
- Conv quantized (select H100): p95=170ms, p99=350ms, accuracy delta approx -0.9

Cost projection (monthly, steady mix):
- Baseline: $38,100/mo (compute + infra + headroom buffer)
- With recommendations (cache + batching + 10% quant canary): $28,700–30,500/mo projected (20–25% savings)

Recommendations (practical runbook to propose to Nebula):
1) Immediate (can be done in 1 sprint):
   - Enable prefix KV caching for ingestion route with aggressive TTL refresh on warm shards (reduce cold-window impact).
   - Configure model preload windows during predicted traffic peaks (staggered across nodes).
   - Route conv-hot shards to H100s and set A100s primarily as warm standby and quant-run candidates.
2) Near-term (2–6 weeks):
   - Introduce route-based batching policy: small window (15–25ms) for conv baseline, dynamic bump to 35–45ms during low-load periods to improve batch efficiency. Instrument per-route latency budgets.
   - Canary deploy conv-llm-q4a at 10% traffic to measure production accuracy drift and kernel stability across node classes.
   - Tune autoscaler threshold to proactively spin up hot nodes on burst-detection (burst detector: 3x baseline qps sustained >20s).
3) Operational (process + metrics):
   - Add synthetic canary that runs every 5 minutes to verify conv SLO and cache hit ratios; auto-rollback if p95 > 270ms for 3 consecutive checks.
   - Add cost telemetry per-route in Redwood Console (token-level cost, model-version breakdown).

Tradeoffs and open questions for Nebula to consider:
- Batching vs latency trade: larger batching windows improve cost but widen variance and can inflate p99 during bursts. Nebula must decide whether 99th percentile stability or lower median latency is primary for end users.
- Quantization acceptance threshold: accept small accuracy delta for 20–25% cost savings? Need product signoff and longer A/B on production prompt set.
- Hardware standardization: mixing H100 and A100 saved capital but complicates quantized routing. If Nebula prioritizes quantized steady-state, prefer single-class pool or enforced kernel parity.

Appendix: short checklist for next workshop with Nebula engineers (action-oriented)
- [ ] Run extended 7-day canary for conv-llm-q4a at 10% traffic and capture model-level accuracy deltas per prompt cluster
- [ ] Implement staggered pre-warm script and validate model load spread across 10-minute windows
- [ ] Prototype dynamic batching controller that adjusts window by queue depth and target p95
- [ ] Prepare customer-facing one-pager summarizing cost/latency tradeoffs for exec review

Meeting notes / informal observations:
- Nebula team emphasized user-facing interactivity for triage flows; they prefer p95 guarantees over lower median if tradeoff is needed.
- Solutions team observed that telemetry ingestion is extremely forgiving to quantization; easiest cost-win pathway is classifying ingestion then offloading long-tail convs to quantized pool.

Unresolved items and follow-ups:
- Confirm production prompt set acceptance criteria for conv quantization A/B (Nebula Product to provide definitive list).
- Validate kernel versions across Nebula’s A100 fleet; ops to provide CUDA driver matrix.
- Finalize committed capacity sizing if Nebula wants to guarantee 99.9% availability during 5x microbursts.

Author notes: this document mixes crisp numbers from runs and workshop discussion fragments; treat as solutions-engineering synthesis draft. Next update should add 7-day canary results and a short executive one-page for Nebula procurement.
